# Delete static LDAP roles

Vault does not rotate passwords when you delete a static role. We recommend
manually rotating the mapped credentials before deleting the role or revoking
access to the static role.

<Tip title="Assumptions">

- You have [set up an `ldap` plugin](/vault/docs/secrets/ldap/setup). 
- You have permission to delete the static role in Vault.

</Tip>

Deletion removes the role from Vault; it does not delete the LDAP account.
Replace `<mount>` and `<name>` with the mount path and role name. You do not
need a configuration file to delete a role.

<Tabs>

<Tab heading="CLI" group="cli">

@include 'ldap/delete-static-role/cli.mdx'

Confirm deletion by listing the roles, if your policy grants `list`:

```shell-session
$ vault list <mount>/static-role
```

The deleted role no longer appears in the list.

</Tab>

<Tab heading="API" group="api">

@include 'ldap/delete-static-role/api.mdx'

Confirm deletion by listing the roles, if your policy grants `list`:

```shell-session
$ curl \
    --request LIST \
    --header "X-Vault-Token: ${VAULT_TOKEN}" \
    ${VAULT_ADDR}/v1/<mount>/static-role
```

The deleted role no longer appears in the list.

</Tab>

<Tab heading="GUI" group="gui">

These steps apply to root-managed and self-managed static roles. Your policy
must grant `read` and `delete` on `<mount>/static-role/<name>`. The GUI hides
**Delete role** when you do not have the deletion permission.

1. Open the Vault GUI, go to **Secrets engines**, and select your LDAP mount.

1. Open the **Roles** tab and select the static role.

1. Click **Manage**, then **Delete role**.

1. In the **Are you sure?** dialog, click **Confirm**. You cannot recover the
   deleted role.

The GUI displays **Role deleted successfully.** and returns to the **Roles**
tab. Click **Cancel** in the confirmation dialog to keep the role.

</Tab>

</Tabs>
